name: Tour de Scottsdale
start_location: WestWorld of Scottsdale, 16601 N Pima Rd, Scottsdale, AZ 85260
date_note: The ride is Saturday, April 10, 2027. The weekend runs Thursday to Saturday at WestWorld: the Prologue with the pros, then packet pick-up and the expo on Friday from noon to 8:00 pm, then the ride.
typical_timing: A Saturday in spring since the 2024 return (March 28 in 2026, April 12 in 2025, April 13 in 2024). Before the pause it was an October ride.

organizer.name: McDowell Sonoran Conservancy with Perimeter Bicycling Association of America (El Tour America)

registration_note: Registration opened September 17, 2026 and closes Friday, April 9, 2027 at 8:00 pm, or earlier if it fills. No day-of registration. Adults pay $115 through December 31, 2026, $130 through March 31, 2027 and $140 after that; military and first responders $100; under 18 $40; VIP $250 with a front corral, the jersey and a cap. No refunds and no deferrals; it runs rain or shine. The organizer lowered the 2027 fee and dropped the day-of lunch to do it.

distances.label: 54 miles
distances.note: 7:00 am start. Around the McDowell Mountains through Scottsdale, Rio Verde and Fountain Hills. Timed, with Platinum corrals for Cat 1, Cat 2 and qualified riders

distances.label: The Prologue
distances.note: A ride with Bobby Julich, Frankie Andreu and Leanda Cave in the days before. Its own entry on BikeSignup

terrain: Paved roads, open to traffic, around the McDowell Mountains: Pima Rd north from WestWorld, Dynamite Blvd, Rio Verde Dr, past McDowell Mountain Park to Fountain Hills Blvd and Shea Blvd, then back in on Via Linda and Frank Lloyd Wright Blvd (the 2026 roads; 2027's maps go up on Ride with GPS by March 1)
participants: about 2,700 in 2024, from 41 states and five countries; more than 3,000 expected in 2025 and 2026, per the organizer and the city
cost: $115–$140 for adults depending on when you sign up (2027 pricing); $100 military and first responders; $40 under 18; $250 VIP
summary: The Tour de Scottsdale is a timed charity ride on Saturday, April 10, 2027, with 54- and 28-mile routes that start and finish at WestWorld of Scottsdale. The long route goes around the McDowell Mountains through Rio Verde and Fountain Hills; the short one stays in Scottsdale. The McDowell Sonoran Conservancy and Perimeter Bicycling, the people behind El Tour de Tucson, run it, HonorHealth is the title sponsor, and riders can raise money for any of 30-plus nonprofits. It started in 2004, paused after 2019 and came back in 2024 with about 2,700 riders.
history: The first Tour de Scottsdale was in 2004. For years it was an October ride that rolled out of Market Street at DC Ranch at 5:00 am, close to 2,000 riders strong, raising money for the McDowell Sonoran Conservancy, the group that looks after the preserve the ride circles. The 2014 edition was the eleventh; the 2013 ride raised close to $50,000 for the Conservancy.

The 2019 ride was the last before a five-year pause. In September 2023 El Tour de Tucson's organizer, Perimeter Bicycling, and the Conservancy announced it was coming back, with HonorHealth as the title sponsor and a move to spring. The comeback ride on April 13, 2024 drew just over 2,700 riders from 41 states and five countries. George Hincapie rode in the lead group; the fastest woman, Caitlin Kellog, rides for Bicycle Haüs in Old Town.

The 2025 and 2026 rides were 62 and 32 miles. For 2027 the organizer cut the courses to 54 and 28 miles, lowered the entry fee and dropped the day-of lunch to keep the ride affordable. More than 20 nonprofits fundraise through it; the Conservancy is one of them, not the only one.
what_to_expect: Everything is at WestWorld: packet pick-up and the expo on Friday, April 9 from noon to 8:00 pm in the North Hall, or Saturday from 5:30 to 6:30 am if you missed it. Parking at WestWorld is free; the organizer says to allow extra time for it on the morning. The 54-mile ride starts at 7:00 am, the 28 at 8:15. The Platinum riders (Cat 1, Cat 2 and the qualified) go first after a Friday meeting at 1:00 or 6:00 pm.

The roads are open to traffic. There are no closures; you ride by the traffic laws unless an official on the course says otherwise, and you yield to emergency vehicles even where a road has been closed. The course and all support close at 2:00 pm; anyone still out gets stopped and driven to the finish, and riders far behind may be sent onto a shorter route. Aid stations are the only places a friend can hand you anything. CPSC helmets are required, aero bars are banned, and so are headphones that cover both ears. E-bikes are welcome but get no placement awards and no Platinum corral.

The long route in 2026 went up Pima Rd past Thompson Peak Parkway, out Dynamite Blvd to Rio Verde Dr, past McDowell Mountain Park, into Fountain Hills on Fountain Hills Blvd and back west on Shea Blvd, Via Linda and Frank Lloyd Wright Blvd to WestWorld. Expect long desert roads, a cool start and a warm finish. The post-ride party runs 10:00 am to 2:00 pm with food trucks, a beer garden and a DJ; the expo closes at 4:00.
weather_note: Around April 10 Scottsdale averages a high of about 83°F and a low of about 58°F, with roughly a 5 percent chance of rain on any given day and a light wind out of the west. Sunrise is close to 6:00 am, so the 7:00 start is cool and the finish is warm. Drink early.

faq.q: When is the Tour de Scottsdale 2027?
faq.a: Saturday, April 10, 2027. Packet pick-up and the expo are Friday, April 9 at WestWorld from noon to 8:00 pm. The 54-mile ride starts at 7:00 am, the 28-mile at 8:15 am.
WestWorld of Scottsdale, 16601 N Pima Rd, in north Scottsdale. Both routes start and finish there, and the expo and the post-ride party are there too. Parking is free.

Adults pay $115 through December 31, 2026, $130 through March 31, 2027 and $140 after that. Military and first responders pay $100, riders under 18 pay $40, VIP is $250. Registration closes April 9 at 8:00 pm; there is no day-of registration and no refunds.

faq.q: How long are the routes, and how hard?
faq.a: 54 miles around the McDowell Mountains through Rio Verde and Fountain Hills, or 28 miles inside Scottsdale. The organizer posts the 2027 maps on Ride with GPS by March 1. The 2024 version of the long route, at 62 miles, had 3,383 feet of climbing.
Yes. The ride and all course support close at 2:00 pm. Riders still on the course are stopped and driven to the finish.
Yes. E-bikes are allowed under Arizona law but are not eligible for placement awards, the Platinum division or Platinum qualifying.

The host hotel is the Hilton Garden Inn Scottsdale North Perimeter Center, 2.2 miles from the start, with a room block under the name Tour de Scottsdale. Five other hotels within four miles hold blocks too, and WestWorld's own RV park has 398 spaces with water and electric at $57.01 a night (Oct 2026). The Scottsdale guide has the hotels.
Riders fundraise for the nonprofit they pick from the event's list, 30-plus of them, the McDowell Sonoran Conservancy among them. Fundraising is through the event's own site, never through this one.
